channel.title: mint - companies
channel.description: Get the latest news and analysis on business, finance, politics from mint, the website of the Mint newspaper, one of India's leading business and financial dailies

item.title: SpaceX-Tesla merger: Elon Musk’s companies assemble teams to discuss ‘biggest ever’ $3.2 trillion deal
item.description: Tesla and SpaceX have formed committees, with five directors and three investment banks, to evaluate a potential $3.2 trillion all-stock merger. The companies are reportedly negotiating a deal that could be announced as soon as December.

item.title: Nvidia all-hands meeting: Jensen Huang tells employees he is in therapy, still doesn’t believe in a succession plan
item.description: Jensen Huang apologized to Nvidia employees after returning as CEO, saying he had made serious mistakes and was in therapy. He denied political pressure behind his reinstatement and rejected claims he was above the law. Huang also defended Nvidia’s lack of a succession plan.

item.title: Investors, proxy firms question fairness of APL Apollo's ₹28k-cr Tata Steel deal
item.description: The key concern lies in the complex structuring of the deal, where APL Apollo will buy two assets from Tata Steel for a total ₹28,000 crore, funded through debt. Tata Steel, in turn, will pay ₹15,510 crore for the 26.38% promoter stake in the tubes firm and make an open offer for another 26% stake.

item.title: Exclusive: Two Mistry letters to govt, 16 RBI meetings—inside the Tata Sons listing push
item.description: An RTI-based Mint investigation found that Shapoorji Pallonji Group chairman Shapoor Mistry pressed the government for an IPO of Tata Sons. RBI records also revealed 16 meetings between the RBI’s top officials and Tata leaders since 2022.

item.title: HPE shares tumble as shrinking AI margins overshadow upbeat forecast
item.description: HPE-STOCKS:HPE shares tumble as shrinking AI margins overshadow upbeat forecast

item.title: Sanofi’s $41 Billion Insmed Deal Shows Cost of a Patent Cliff
item.description: Sanofi SA’s $41 billion purchase of Insmed Inc. shows the high cost of waiting to plug the gaps in Big Pharma’s drug pipeline.

item.title: Can Amazon’s Trainium chips reduce its dependence on Nvidia? The Decart acquisition offers clues
item.description: Amazon is acquiring AI startup Decart’s technology and hiring its founders and staff, aiming to strengthen its Trainium chips against Nvidia. Decart’s software helps optimize AI workloads across different hardware, potentially easing customers’ transition between chip platforms.

item.title: Volkswagen seeks 2-year pay freeze for 120,000 workers as union threatens strikes from Jan 1
item.description: Volkswagen has proposed a two-year pay freeze and cuts to employee benefits for 120,000 workers in Germany, prompting union IG Metall to threaten strikes from January 1, 2027, if negotiations fail.

item.title: OpenAI spying case: Ex-engineer allegedly stole trade secrets, recorded meetings, and kept confidential document
item.description: In a court filing on Monday, prosecutors said investigators had recovered hundreds of audio files from Alfozan's personal computer, including dozens of recordings of meetings and conversations at OpenAI during September 2026.

item.title: Why Karnataka drivers' unions oppose Nitin Gadkari's push for private two-wheelers as Rapido, Uber, Ola bike taxis
item.description: Karnataka drivers' unions have opposed Nitin Gadkari's proposal to allow private two-wheelers as Rapido, Uber, and Ola bike taxis, citing concerns about livelihoods, unfair competition and passenger safety. They argue that private vehicles should face the same commercial regulations as taxis.&nbsp;

item.title: Jensen Huang back as Nvidia CEO: What his return means for Colette Kress after her 11-day stint as interim CEO
item.description: Nvidia reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO and board president after an 11-day interim leadership period under CFO Colette Kress. The board said his return posed no national security risk, despite its investigation remaining incomplete. Kress is expected to resume her CFO duties.

item.title: Shadowfax buys WeFast for ₹23 crore to enter intra-city logistics
item.description: The acquisition gives Shadowfax access to a market valued at $15 billion, where nearly 70% of activity is still handled by unorganized operators.

item.title: Pixxel’s big Bengaluru bet: Inside the startup’s plan to build 2.5 lakh sq ft satellite factory near Kempegowda airport
item.description: Pixxel will set up a 2.5 lakh sq ft satellite manufacturing facility near Bengaluru’s Kempegowda airport. The GigaPixxel unit aims to produce 50 satellites simultaneously by mid-2027, scaling to 200 by mid-2028, boosting Karnataka’s spacetech ecosystem.

item.title: Tata Sons wins ITAT backing for ₹1,498 crore interest deduction on group investments
item.description: The ITAT ruled that Tata Sons may deduct interest on loans used to invest in group companies, subject to limits for expenses linked to tax-exempt income. It said the company’s activities extend beyond passively earning dividends and that its business purpose must be considered.

item.title: Megaspeed blacklisted by US over alleged Nvidia chip diversion to China; Here's what it means
item.description: The US Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS), which operates under the Department of Commerce, on Monday placed Megaspeed International and six other companies in Southeast Asia on its Entity List, citing concerns that they were acting contrary to US national security or foreign policy interests.

item.title: AERA rejects GMR’s distance-based user development fees proposal at Bhogapuram airport
item.description: The regulator has rejected GMR’s proposal to vary passenger fees by travel distance, but approved domestic departure charges that are significantly higher than at the other two new greenfield airports.

item.title: Tata Sons reviews Air India, Tata Digital and Tata Electronics after Noel Tata flags losses of nearly ₹29,000 crore
item.description: Tata Sons chairman N Chandrasekaran has begun reviewing businesses flagged by Noel Tata over mounting losses. After Air India, the review is expected to cover Tata’s Dholera semiconductor project, as the group assesses turnaround plans.

item.title: Who is Neil Mehta? Why is the Indian-origin billionaire donating ₹55.72 crore to Trump Accounts?
item.description: The message accompanying the Mehtas' contribution in the Trump Accounts programme read: ‘The future is going to be wild and wonderful. Own a piece of it.’

item.title: Ashok Leyland turns to Bengal for manufacturing expansion: What is the company planning to make in Singur? Details here
item.description: Union minister Sukanta Majumdar says Ashok Leyland will build a heavy-vehicle plant in Singur, where a planned Tata Nano factory was abandoned after protests over land acquisition. The announcement follows initial talks with the company, but project details remain unclear.

item.title: Spotify outage: Music streaming service back online after more than 16,000 users report problems
item.description: Spotify acknowledged the disruption in a post on X, saying it was aware of the issues and was investigating them. However, the company subsequently indicated that the situation was improving, suggesting that services were gradually returning to normal.

item.title: GSK India enters blood cancer space with Blenrep launch, bets on new drugs for growth
item.description: The launch of its third oncology drug expands GSK’s innovative medicines portfolio as it targets doubling revenue to ₹8,000 crore by FY30, with new assets expected to contribute at least 20% to overall revenue.

item.title: IDBI Bank stake sale: Bank employees threaten strike on December 3 against Fairfax deal; Here’s what they demand
item.description: The proposed sale involves the transfer of a combined 60.72 per cent stake in IDBI Bank held by the government and Life Insurance Corporation of India (LIC) to Fairfax Financial Holdings.

item.title: Ventive plans ₹1,350 crore hotel expansion without fresh equity
item.description: Ventive Hospitality targets ₹2,000–2,200 crore in operating earnings by FY31, with growth led mainly by its existing hotels.

item.title: Uday Kotak on Jensen Huang coming back as NVIDIA CEO: ‘When elephants dance, everyone moves to give space!’ - Full text
item.description: Uday Kotak described Nvidia’s decision to reinstate co-founder Jensen Huang as CEO as consequential for global markets, linking it to the AI race and shifting geopolitical priorities. Nvidia shares and Taiwan’s Taiex rallied after the board unanimously approved Huang’s return.

item.title: TSMC stock jumps 10%, adds $158 billion in market value as Nvidia's Jensen Huang returns as CEO
item.description: The rally came after Nvidia shares surged 31.48% on Monday, adding nearly $950 billion to the company's market value, after its board unanimously reinstated Huang as president and chief executive with immediate effect.

item.title: IKEA pushes India profitability target to FY29 as losses persist
item.description: The delayed profitability timeline comes as IKEA India continues to invest in expansion, even as it makes progress in improving its financial performance.

item.title: Slurrp Farm parent eyes majority stake sale at up to ₹2,000 crore valuation
item.description: Wholsum Foods, which operates Slurrp Farm and Mille, has approached players like Nestle and ITC, and even European buyers

item.title: Mint Explainer: Can SpiceJet raise ₹5,500 crore to stay afloat?
item.description: SpiceJet is struggling to pay aircraft lessors, salaries and small suppliers. Without the financial lifeline, the airline's survival could be at risk.

item.title: Before returning as CEO, Jensen Huang told Nvidia board of additional affairs beyond two reported | What we know
item.description: Nvidia has reinstated CEO Jensen Huang, 11 days after he stepped down amid revelations about his extramarital relationships. The decision followed intervention by Donald Trump, support from Elon Musk and other tech leaders, and assurances from the Justice Department.

item.title: Not just Donald Trump, JD Vance used his Silicon Valley connections to get Jensen Huang back as Nvidia’s CEO
item.description: Jensen Huang has returned as Nvidia CEO after the board reversed its decision to remove him. Reports say President Trump and senior officials urged the board to reinstate him, citing national security concerns and the importance of US leadership in open-weight AI.&nbsp;

item.title: No successor in sight: What Jensen Huang’s return reveals about Nvidia’s leadership challenges
item.description: Nvidia added nearly $1 trillion in market value after Huang's return, while the rally boosted the value of his personal stake by about $32 billion, according to the Bloomberg Billionaires Index. The estimate is based on his 3.4% ownership of the company.

item.title: Cashing in on nostalgia! In pics: From Campa Cola to Gold Spot, iconic Indian soft drink brands that have made comeback
item.description: Gold Spot, once a popular Indian orange soda, may return to shelves after more than two decades, according to reports. Though Coca-Cola has not formally announced the revival, the brand would join Campa Cola and Thums Up among homegrown drinks that have made successful comebacks.

item.title: ‘IDBI Bank’ not ‘State’ under Article 12, rules Supreme Court; dismisses appeal by association | What we know
item.description: The Supreme Court has ruled that IDBI Bank is not 'State' under Article 12 of the Constitution, dismissing appeals by its officers' association. The decision comes amid the proposed sale of over 60% stake by the Centre and LIC, and concerns over employee and pension benefits.

item.title: ‘Portfolio rebalancing’: JioStar to lay off around 150 employees this week - what we know
item.description: JioStar plans to lay off about 150 employees across departments, including marketing, production and operations. The company says the cuts are part of a portfolio rebalancing and will provide affected staff with at least six months’ salary and a pro-rata bonus.

item.title: ‘Totally inaccurate’: Google India rejects reports of layoffs in Cloud division, says 30 roles cut as part of changes
item.description: Google has dismissed rumours of widespread layoffs in its India Cloud division as “totally inaccurate”, confirming that around 30 roles were eliminated last week as part of a small organisational change. The clarification follows speculation on X.
